title: Stage A1.1 — Greetings & Introductions
description: Learn to greet people, introduce yourself, and understand basic Spanish sounds.

grammar.title: Articles: el, la, los, las
grammar.content: Spanish has definite articles that agree in gender and number with the noun they modify. Think of them like 'the' in English, but they change based on whether the noun is masculine or feminine, singular or plural.
grammar.aid_note: Like Italian 'il/la/i/le' or French 'le/la/les/les' — gender matters!

grammar.title: Gender of Nouns
grammar.content: Most Spanish nouns are either masculine or feminine. As a general rule: nouns ending in -o are usually masculine, and nouns ending in -a are usually feminine. But there are plenty of exceptions!
grammar.aid_note: Romanian also has grammatical gender (masculine, feminine, neuter) — similar concept!

grammar.title: Introduction to SER
grammar.content: SER is one of two Spanish verbs meaning 'to be.' It's used for permanent characteristics: identity, profession, origin, time, and essential qualities. This is a regular -ER verb.
examples: Soy de España. (I am from Spain.)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian 'a fi' (sunt, ești, este...) is the equivalent 'to be' verb, but SER is more restricted in use than 'a fi'.

pronunciation.title: The Five Vowels
pronunciation.content: Spanish vowels are always pronounced the same way, unlike English where 'a' can sound like many different things. Master these five sounds and you'll be ahead of most beginners.

pronunciation.title: Special Sounds
pronunciation.content: Spanish has a few sounds that don't exist in English. The most important ones for beginners are the rolled 'r' and the 'ñ'.

exercises.question: What is the masculine singular definite article in Spanish?
exercises.explanation: 'El' is the masculine singular definite article (like 'the' for masculine nouns).

exercises.question: Which verb form of SER means 'I am'?
exercises.explanation: 'Soy' is the first-person singular (yo) form of SER.

exercises.question: What gender is the noun 'la casa'?
exercises.explanation: 'La' is the feminine definite article, so 'casa' is feminine.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Yo ___ de España.' (I am from Spain.)
exercises.explanation: 'Soy' is the correct form for 'yo' with SER.

exercises.question: How do you say 'thank you' in Spanish?
Write the plural of 'el libro': el ____
exercises.explanation: Masculine singular nouns ending in a consonant add '-s' to make the plural: el libro → los libros.

exercises.question: The Spanish vowel 'e' is pronounced like:
exercises.explanation: Spanish 'e' is always pronounced like the 'e' in 'bet' — short and crisp.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Me ____ Pablo.' (My name is Pablo.)
exercises.explanation: 'Me llamo' is the standard way to say 'my name is' in Spanish.

exercises.question: What does '¿Cómo estás?' mean?
exercises.explanation: '¿Cómo estás?' literally means 'How are you?' — it's informal. For formal, use '¿Cómo está?'
